title: Evolutionary Information Layering: Multicellularity and the Emergence of Pre-Neural Coordination
content: The Evolutionary Information Layering (EIL) framework describes biological coordination as superimposed informational layers. Its basal Layer 0, pre-neural regulation, was originally treated as a single block. Here I propose that Layer 0 can be examined as a set of proposed functional subdivisions, not established evolutionary stages: ionic or adhesive regulation, junctional and extracellular-matrix coupling, bioelectric patterning, and pre-neural integration (provisional). Multicellularity does not invent coordination; unicellular organisms already sense and regulate. What multicellularity adds is the problem of group-level coordination, in which previously separate regulatory capacities become organizationally coupled (Bozdag et al., 2026). This article refines Layer 0 provisionally, states what the subdivisions are not, and identifies comparative and experimental tests required next. Clinical implications are deferred to a separate series.
